Implementation Plan

I have what the plan needs. Two findings shape it:

- **Conflict with the issue wording.** The issue says to take the cycle from the comments the script "already fetches" (`PRIOR_COMMENTS`). That read only runs once the cycle is above 1, so it can't be used to work the cycle out in the first place. It also keeps only comment bodies, with no author. Derivation therefore needs one new paginated read that keeps the author.
- **The escalation can still miss.** Even with the right cycle number, `PRIOR_COMMENTS` keeps only the last 3 "Runtime validation" comments. At cycle 3 that window can leave out cycle 1's fingerprint marker. I've flagged this rather than widening the scope.

## Files likely to change
- `scripts/validate_process.sh`
- `tests/test_validate_process_cross_cycle_escalation.py`
- `agents.d/validation-harness-routing-p4.md` (new)
- `changelog.d/validation-harness-routing-p4.md` (new)

## Functions or modules to implement

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends validation_owner_pipeline_login
Scope-mode justification: The issue covers Phase 4 of `docs/plans/validation-failure-harness-routing-plan.md` only: work out `VALIDATION_CYCLE` when it is not set. The plan reuses the pipeline-login lookup that the P1c owner-routing block already memoizes (`validation_owner_pipeline_login`). It copies the stub-`gh` sandbox test pattern from `tests/test_validate_process_owner_routing.py`. It changes no workflow, wrapper or input (Q11). The `PRIOR_COMMENTS` window issue found while reading (see Risks) is noted for the tracking project, not fixed here. Fixing it would change how the escalation scans comments, which is outside this issue.

Planning ref: `HEAD` 636a82aaf93b248b5e665f0d5dc76f45f236b902 on `orchestrator/project-7913` (Integration branch mismatch: false).

1. **`scripts/validate_process.sh` ~line 209 (defaulting).**
   - Before the existing `VALIDATION_CYCLE="${VALIDATION_CYCLE:-1}"` line, record whether an explicit value was given: `VALIDATION_CYCLE_EXPLICIT=true` when `${VALIDATION_CYCLE:-}` is non-empty, else `false`.
   - Also record `VALIDATION_CYCLE_INVALID_ENV=true` when the existing positive-integer check resets a non-empty value to 1.
   - Keep the existing default to 1 and the existing warning byte-identical. Every early failure path that prints `cycle=${VALIDATION_CYCLE}` keeps a valid integer.

2. **New block** `# BEGIN validation cycle derivation (project #7913 p4)` … `# END validation cycle derivation`. Place it directly after `# END validation owner routing` (~line 2676). At that point `RUNTIME_DIR`, `gh_retry`, `is_tracking_run` and `validation_owner_pipeline_login` all exist. It runs before the `PRIOR_FAILURE_CONTEXT_FILE` / `PRIOR_COMMENTS` fetch (~4475) and the escalation gate (~5299), so both see the worked-out cycle.
   - The block defines `validation_cycle_resolve()` and calls it once at top level, as its last line.
   - **Explicit value** (`VALIDATION_CYCLE_EXPLICIT=true`):
     - Valid: log `VALIDATION_CYCLE_SOURCE source=env cycle=N` and return. No API call.
     - Invalid (`VALIDATION_CYCLE_INVALID_ENV=true`): log `source=default cycle=1 reason=invalid_env`. Don't derive; this keeps today's behaviour for a bad explicit value.
   - **Not a tracking run** (`is_tracking_run` false): log `source=default cycle=1 reason=not_tracking_run`. No API call.
   - **Login:** `login="$(validation_owner_pipeline_login)"`. On failure, log `source=default cycle=1 reason=login_unavailable`. This reuses the memoized `gh api user` read, so there is at most one identity call per run, shared with P1c.
   - **Comments:** one paginated read, with a §14 audit comment above it saying the existing `PRIOR_COMMENTS` read is gated on cycle > 1, keeps bodies only and has no author:

     ```
     gh_retry gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${TRACKING_ISSUE_NUM}/comments?per_page=100" --paginate \
       --jq '.[] | select(((.body // "") | split("\n")[0] | sub("\r$"; "")) == "## 🧪 Runtime validation dispatched") | {login: (.user.login // ""), body: (.body // "")} | @json'
     ```

     It keeps one JSON item per comment, so there's no per-page `.[-3:]` quirk. On failure, log `source=default cycle=1 reason=comments_unavailable`.
   - **Parse:** `jq -rs --arg login "$login"` keeps only items whose `.login == $login`, takes the last one (comments come in ascending creation order), splits its body into lines, strips trailing `\r`/whitespace, and returns the first line matching `^- Cycle: [0-9]+$`, minus the prefix.
     - Accept only `^[1-9][0-9]{0,5}$` (positive integer, bounded so shell arithmetic can't overflow).
     - No trusted comment: `source=default cycle=1 reason=no_dispatch_comment`.
     - Newest trusted comment has no valid line: `source=default cycle=1 reason=malformed_cycle`. Don't fall back to an older comment.
     - Valid: set `VALIDATION_CYCLE=N` and log `VALIDATION_CYCLE_SOURCE source=dispatch_comment cycle=N`.
   - **Failure handling:** every jq/gh failure is caught (`|| …`) so `set -e`/`pipefail` can't abort the script. The function always returns 0.

3. **No other edits.** The `PRIOR_COMMENTS` fetch line, the escalation block and the workflow files are unchanged.

## Data structures affected
- New shell globals: `VALIDATION_CYCLE_EXPLICIT`, `VALIDATION_CYCLE_INVALID_ENV`, and the function `validation_cycle_resolve`. The implementer must `grep -n` the script and its sourced helpers (`gh_helpers.sh`, `codex_helpers.sh`, `watchdog_helpers.sh`, `write_guard.sh`) to confirm none of these names exists yet.
- `VALIDATION_CYCLE` can now be above 1 on runs where it isn't set (consumers, and this repo, since `validate.yml` doesn't set it).
- No state, schema or memory record changes.

## API or interface changes
- New stable log line: `VALIDATION_CYCLE_SOURCE source=<env|dispatch_comment|default> cycle=N`. A `source=default` line also carries `reason=<invalid_env|not_tracking_run|login_unavailable|comments_unavailable|no_dispatch_comment|malformed_cycle>`. The `reason=` field goes beyond the issue's format; it is additive and helps operators.
- GitHub API: one new paginated comments read per tracking run without an explicit cycle. The identity read reuses P1c's memoized `gh api user` (one call per run at most). No writes.
- No workflow input, wrapper or env var change (Q11).

## Decisions

### D1 — Separate author-aware read instead of reusing `PRIOR_COMMENTS`
- Chosen: one new paginated read that keeps `{login, body}` of dispatch comments, run before the existing fetch.
- Alternatives considered:
  - Parse `PRIOR_COMMENTS` itself, as the issue literally says.
  - Restructure the existing fetch into one shared author-aware read.
- Why:
  - `PRIOR_COMMENTS` is only fetched when the cycle is already above 1, so it can't be used to derive the cycle.
  - It has no author, so the trust filter can't be applied.
  - Restructuring would change the long-standing `--paginate`/`.[-3:]` behaviour and the literal `PRIOR_COMMENTS="$(gh_retry gh api` line that `test_prior_fingerprint_scan_uses_existing_prior_comments_fetch` pins.

### D2 — Only the newest trusted dispatch comment counts
- Chosen: newest pipeline-login dispatch comment; if its `Cycle:` line is malformed, fall back to 1.
- Alternatives considered: walk back to an older valid comment.
- Why:
  - The issue says a malformed line falls back to 1.
  - `/revalidate` and recovery resets post `Cycle: 1`. Walking back could revive a stale higher cycle.

### D3 — An invalid explicit value is not derived
- Chosen: an explicit but invalid `VALIDATION_CYCLE` keeps today's warning and 1, logged as `source=default reason=invalid_env`.
- Alternatives considered: derive from the comment when the explicit value is invalid.
- Why: the issue says to derive only when the value is unset or empty, and an explicit caller's intent should not be silently replaced (§2.1 preserve behaviour).

## Security considerations
- **Trust boundary:** tracking-issue comments are untrusted. Only comments whose `user.login` equals the pipeline login (the authenticated `GH_PAT` account, via `validation_owner_pipeline_login`) count. An outsider posting "## 🧪 Runtime validation dispatched / - Cycle: 99" is ignored.
- **Input validation:** the cycle must match `^[1-9][0-9]{0,5}$` before it enters shell arithmetic. This prevents injection (no `eval`, values passed as jq `--arg`) and arithmetic overflow.
- **Abuse cases:**
  - A forged high cycle could force an early `harness_error` escalation. This is blocked by the author filter.
  - A comment body is never echoed into the log; only the parsed integer and fixed reason tokens are printed.
- **Authorization and secrets:** no new endpoints or writes; no secrets logged. A failed identity read fails open to cycle 1, which is today's behaviour. That direction is safe: it only means no escalation.
- **Money handling:** not applicable.

## Potential risks or edge cases
- **Escalation window (conflict, out of scope).** The existing `PRIOR_COMMENTS` read keeps only the last 3 "Runtime validation" bodies (per page, because `--jq` runs on each page under `--paginate`). The dispatch comments themselves match that filter. So at cycle 3 the window typically holds dispatched(c2), failed(c2), dispatched(c3), and cycle 1's `validation-failure-fingerprint … cycle: 1` marker is missing. The escalation can then still not fire in production even with the correct cycle. This needs a follow-up: widen the window or scan markers from a trusted read.
- **Behaviour change in consumers.** A cycle above 1 now:
  - fetches prior-failure context and injects it into the generate prompt (intended);
  - numbers consolidated fix-up local IDs, titles and the dedupe text "at cycle N" with the real cycle;
  - sends a real `validation_cycle` in the self-heal dispatch payload.
- **Token type.** If a consumer's validate job ran with `github.token` rather than `GH_PAT`, `gh api user` fails. This falls back to 1, logged `reason=login_un
